levels.name: Level 0
levels.desc: There are gaps in the organisation's overall security posture. One or more strategies are not implemented, leaving weaknesses an adversary could exploit.

levels.name: Level 1
levels.desc: A baseline aimed at adversaries using common, widely available tools and techniques. A good first target for most organisations.

levels.name: Level 2
levels.desc: Aimed at adversaries willing to invest more time and effort, and to bypass or evade some controls. Appropriate where the impact of compromise is higher.

levels.name: Level 3
levels.desc: Aimed at highly capable, adaptive adversaries. Suited to organisations that are a high-value target or hold especially sensitive data.

strategies.name: Application control
levels: Not implemented, or only on some workstations.
Execution of executables, scripts, installers and similar is restricted to an approved set on workstations.
Applied to workstations and internet-facing servers, with allowed and blocked execution events centrally logged.
Applied across workstations and servers, using the recommended block rules, with rulesets validated annually and logs protected.

strategies.name: Patch applications
levels: Patching is slow, inconsistent, or untracked.
Internet-facing applications patched within two weeks, or 48 hours when an exploit exists; unsupported apps removed.
Other applications patched within a month, with regular vulnerability scanning of internet-facing services.
Internet-facing exploited vulnerabilities patched within 48 hours; frequent scanning; no unsupported software in use.

strategies.name: Configure Office macros
levels: Macros run freely for everyone.
Macros are blocked for users who do not have a demonstrated business need.
Allowed macros run only from trusted locations or are digitally signed, with macro security settings enforced.
Only macros signed by trusted publishers run, with antivirus scanning and macro events centrally logged.

strategies.name: User application hardening
levels: Applications run on their default configurations.
Web browsers block ads, Java and Flash content; internet-facing features are reduced.
Browsers, Office and PDF readers are hardened to guidance, with settings enforced and events logged.
Broad, enforced hardening across the environment, with unneeded features blocked and events centrally logged.

strategies.name: Restrict admin privileges
levels: Privileged access is broad and rarely reviewed.
Privileged access requests are validated, and privileged accounts cannot access the internet, email or web services.
Privileged access is limited to what duties require, used in a separate environment, and revalidated regularly.
Just-in-time administration, secure admin workstations, and strong separation with full logging.

strategies.name: Patch operating systems
levels: Operating systems are patched slowly, and end-of-life systems remain in use.
Internet-facing OS vulnerabilities patched within two weeks, or 48 hours when exploited; unsupported OSes removed.
All operating systems patched within a month, with regular scanning to find missing patches.
Exploited internet-facing OS vulnerabilities patched within 48 hours; frequent scanning; no unsupported operating systems.

strategies.name: Multi-factor authentication
levels: MFA is not used, or only in a few places.
MFA is used by users on internet-facing services that handle sensitive data.
MFA is phishing-resistant for privileged users and applied to all users of internet-facing services, with events logged.
Phishing-resistant MFA is used broadly, including for important data repositories, with successful and failed events logged.

strategies.name: Regular backups
levels: No regular or reliable backups.
Backups of important data, software and settings are performed and retained in line with business needs.
Backups are synchronised, access is restricted, and restoration is tested as part of disaster recovery exercises.
Unprivileged accounts cannot access, modify or delete backups, and restoration is tested regularly.
